items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: The only singer we hired was with Pierron, the boy named Harry Wells. We hired him when he was on the boat to sing with us.

ctx.x: Who would do the singing in the band? Oh, different fellas. Sing.

Buddy never did sing. None of them didn't sing in the band. The only singer we hired was with Pierron, the boy named Harry Wells. We hired him when he was on the boat to sing with us. And I was with Pichon on the Pelican in 1928 and Raymond Brown and all of us. Pichon sang. Raymond would sing. What about Sam?
Did he sing any? Yeah, he'd sing that, yeah. I heard him on the record. I thought he could sing in person.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I played with P-Rom's band from 32 to 35... And Harry Wells was our singer.

ctx.x: How did Sales rate in those days? He was a nice, fine guitar player. I just wondered who would be among the best guitar players in town. Oh yeah, he was fine, yes indeed.

He always was a musician, you see. He learned the right way. Oh yeah, a musician. That's what I did. He was great, good. Always have been. What about P-Rom's band? P-Rom's band? I played with P-Rom's band from 32 to 35. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with with Song that was after that. He broke up the band. Now his band consists of P. Ron's band, when I first started playing, consists of me, P. Ron, Lil' Allegrette Alexander, Eddie Pearson on trombone,…
